chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Amr ibn al-Afraq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is befitting for the two believers that when one of them is hidden from his companion by a tree, then they meet, they should shake hands.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for Muslims when meeting after a short separation?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the handshake from a mere greeting to a spiritual act of reaffirming brotherhood (ukhuwwah) and dispelling any latent resentment. Scholars note that the specific imagery of being 'obscured by a tree' highlights the need for conscious re-engagement after even brief physical or social separation, ensuring that the bond of faith remains visibly active and warm.
